content.value: A single Go binary that terminates TLS once and routes every public path on the box to the right backend.
Caddy is the front door on Production: one statically-linked Go binary holding a single ACME certificate for

reaches the Bulldocs reader; everything else falls through to Phoenix.
Caddy exists to own HTTPS so the app doesn't try to. Earlier, Phoenix set
when no HTTPS terminator existed — an infinite 301 loop that returned empty bodies for every API call. Pushing TLS termination out to Caddy and leaving
off cured it. Caddy also keeps answering on its cached cert during a Deploy, so the 60–90s systemd Service restart is invisible to external callers.
